comment: The upstream DSP poptart's browser build ports, as data rather than as prose, so that the
build script, the license report and the planning all read the same list.
Every license here was verified on 2026-09-22 by reading the source rather than the
repository page - which mattered: the Mutable repository declares no license at all, and the
grant is in each file's own header.
status "built" means a binary is committed under public/devices and the device is in the
catalog. "planned" means nothing is built yet.
The web build is AGPL-3.0-only. Everything built so far is MIT, which imposes nothing; the
Faust entry is the one that would make the build permanently copyleft, and it is untouched.
A device with status "retired" was built and then removed from the catalog; its entry stays so the reason is on record.

sources.title: Mutable Instruments
sources.licenseNote: MIT, copyright Emilie Gillet, read from the header of each file used. The repository itself declares no license, so the header is the grant.
sources.notes: Portable C++ over stmlib. Built with -DTEST, which is upstream's own switch for compiling off the target chip: stmlib's inner loops are ARM inline assembly with portable C beside them. Each module renders at its own fixed rate and the wrapper resamples. Tides was ported and then retired: see its entry.

It needs a carrier patched in with .audio(), and after two rounds of wrapper fixes (the fifo feeding it whole 96-frame blocks, and dropping the internal carrier that made it drone through rests) it still produced digital noise across most of its algorithm range. The Wavetable's FM, PM and ring warp modes cover what it was here for. The build script still compiles it.

sources.title: Airwindows
sources.notes: Per-sample C++ against the VST2 SDK, which is not redistributable - so it is compiled against a shim of the handful of declarations these files touch (build/devices/shim/audioeffectx.h). Names, defaults and control counts are read out of each plugin's source at build time. Only Galactic remains in the catalog; the other eight were retired on 2026-09-23 in favor of poptart's own effects, and the build script's list holds only the one.

sources.title: CloudSeed
sources.notes: MOVED: the original repository (ValdemarOrn/CloudSeed) now holds only a readme pointing at the algorithm core, which is published separately and is what this builds. Its label array is out of step with its parameter enum, so the control names are written out here rather than read from it. Needs far more memory than any other device: its delay lines are allocated up front.
sources.licenseNote: MIT, copyright Ghost Note Engineering Ltd.

sources.title: Signalsmith Stretch
sources.notes: Header-only. Only the pitch half is exposed: a track's time belongs to the scheduler. Still wanted as the stretcher behind the sampler's warp modes.
sources.licenseNote: MIT, copyright Signalsmith Audio Ltd. Its signalsmith-linear dependency is MIT as well and is pinned separately.

sources.title: Faust standard library
sources.licenseNote: The license differs PER FUNCTION and is stated in the library source above each one. Several of the reverbs are GPL. Check the function actually used, not the repository.
sources.notes: NOT BEING BUILT, decided 2026-09-23, and the reason is the library rather than the toolchain: the Faust compiler is GPL but exempts what it generates, so compiling with it would not reach this package. The LIBRARY is the risk - its license differs per function, and the reverbs, which are most of what would be wanted here, are the GPL ones. GPL-3 is not allowed in this build, so those are out, and none of the per-function licenses below has been read. Nothing here is built.
